details.description: Devstral Small 2505 is a 24-billion-parameter open-weight coding model that Mistral AI released May 21, 2025 in collaboration with All Hands AI, fine-tuned from Mistral-Small-3.1-24B-Base-2503. It is built for agentic software-engineering work -- exploring codebases and editing multiple files -- through coding-agent scaffolds such as OpenHands and SWE-Agent, and is light enough to run locally on a single RTX 4090 GPU or a Mac with 32GB RAM. Mistral's own current documentation lists this version (internally 'Devstral Small 1.0', API id devstral-small-2505) as deprecated, with a retirement date of November 30, 2025, in favor of later Devstral and Mistral Small/Medium releases.
advantages: Scores 46.8% on SWE-bench Verified, which Mistral describes as a 6-point improvement over the prior open-source state of the art.
Apache 2.0 license permits commercial and non-commercial use and modification.
Small enough to run locally on a single RTX 4090 GPU or a Mac with 32GB RAM, per Mistral.
Supports tool calling for agentic coding frameworks including OpenHands and SWE-Agent.
disadvantages: Mistral's models-overview documentation currently lists this version (devstral-small-2505) as deprecated, with a retirement date of November 30, 2025.
Text-only input and output; the vision encoder was removed from its Mistral-Small-3.1-24B base.
Superseded on Mistral's own roadmap by Devstral Small 1.1 (2507) and Devstral 2, per Mistral's documentation.
use_cases: Agentic software-engineering tasks: codebase exploration, multi-file edits, and bug fixing via coding-agent scaffolds.
Local or on-device deployment for privacy-sensitive repositories.
Integration into IDEs and coding copilots via tool/function calling.

notes: Bud's catalog lists an empty deprecation_date for this target, but Mistral's current models-overview page lists devstral-small-2505 ('Devstral Small 1.0') as deprecated on 2025-10-31 with retirement on 2025-11-30 -- a date already past as of researched_on -- recommending Mistral Medium 3.5 as the replacement. Kept the catalog's facts as-is (context window, modality, endpoints all matched the maker's own pages) but flagged the deprecated/retired status in the description and disadvantages since it materially affects a user's choice.
